title: SRE Resilience Playbook: SLOs, Capacity, and Runbooks
author: Marcus Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook centralizes Redwood Inference’s SRE practices for SLO definition and enforcement, error-budget policy, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, incident review standards, and canonical runbooks. It is the working reference for on-call engineers, SRE project leads, and platform product owners.

Scope
- Applies to Redwood-hosted inference endpoints (text-generation, chat, embeddings) and associated control-plane services (model catalog, routing).
- Includes both production and Dedicated clusters unless explicitly noted.

Key contacts and ownership
- SRE lead: Marcus Chen (marcus.chen@redwood.com)
- Platform product owner: Priya Nambiar (priya.nambiar@redwood.com)
- Oncall rotations: eng-sre oncall (pagerduty: redwood-sre-prod)

1) SLOs and SLIs (definitions and examples)

Principles for SLOs
- User-centric: measure what customers experience (availability, latency, correctness).
- Observable: SLIs must be expressed as queries against production metrics or traces.
- Economical: SLO targets balance user satisfaction and cost (error budget allocation).
- Actionable: SLOs must have clear escalation and remediation playbooks.

SLO catalog (summary)
| Service area | SLI | SLO (rolling 30d) | Alert threshold | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Public text-generation API (/v1/generate) | Successful responses (HTTP 2xx within timeout) | 99.95% availability | 7-day error budget burn > 10% => page | API Platform Team (owner: priya.nambiar@redwood.com) |
| Embeddings API (/v1/embeddings) | Median embedding latency (end-to-end user-visible) | P95 < 200ms | P95 > 300ms for 1 hour => page | Vector Team (owner: diego.alvarez@redwood.com) |
| Control plane (model catalog + routing) | API error rate (5xx) | 99.9% availability | 24h rolling error > 0.1% => slack alert | Platform Core (owner: marcus.chen@redwood.com) |
| Dedicated customer control plane | Provisioning success rate | 99% | Any failed provisioning >= 1% in 24h => page | Private Deployments team |

SLI examples (Prometheus/Observability)
- Availability SLI (generation):
  sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-server", route="/v1/generate"}[30d])) - sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-server", route="/v1/generate", status=~"5..|4.."}[30d]))
  divided by total requests (use exact query in dashboard).
- Latency SLI (P95):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="api-server", route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))

2) Error budget policy and actions

Error budget windows and cadence
- Primary window: rolling 30-day window used for business reporting and quarterly planning.
- Short-term window: rolling 7-day for operational alerts and automated mitigation.

Burn thresholds and automated responses
- Warning: 10% of 30-day budget burned in 7 days. -> Slack alert to #sre-alerts, runbook owner notified, follow-up in 24h.
- Action: 25% burned in 7 days -> PagerDuty page to oncall. Oncall must: (1) assess active incidents, (2) recommend traffic shaping/rollback, (3) notify platform PO.
- Emergency: 50%+ burned in 7 days -> Exec-level escalation, trigger cross-functional incident command (IC) for customer-impact mitigation, freeze non-critical rollouts until budget stabilizes.

Error budget use cases and conservations
- Product features that intentionally degrade latency (e.g., low-cost quantized model) must explicitly reserve error budget in the launch plan and be approved by SRE PO.
- Dedicated customers consuming > 20% of cluster capacity require a separate SLO conversation and a contract-defined SLA.

3) Capacity planning and headroom policy

Targets
- Cluster utilization targets (production inference clusters): sustained CPU/GPU utilization at 55%–65% for cost efficiency.
- Headroom reserve: maintain nominal 30% capacity spare headroom across all clusters to handle burst traffic and failover.
- Autoscaling: autoscaler triggers to keep p95 latency within SLO while maintaining at least 10% instant scaling headroom.

Forecasting process (quarterly)
1. Collect telemetry: monthly QPS, peak-QPS, model mix (tokens/sec), average sequence length, batch efficiency.
2. Convert to GPU-seconds required using benchmark table (see Capacity Calculation example below).
3. Add safety multiplier (1.3 for production).
4. Divide by GPU-hours available per machine to estimate node counts.
5. Validate with runbook-based load tests (canary with 10% of production traffic).

Capacity Calculation example (table)
| Workload | Peak QPS | Avg seq len | Tokens/sec | GPU-seconds/day | GPU nodes (A100 80GB equiv) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Gen-api (prod-east) | 1,200 | 128 | 153,600 | 13,000 | 12 |
| Embeddings (prod-west) | 4,500 | 32 | 144,000 | 9,500 | 9 |

Operational runway and procurements
- Procurement lead times: GPUs and cloud commitments require at least 8 weeks planning for normal growth, 16+ weeks for specialized procurement.
- Reserved vs spot mix: baseline reserved capacity for 70% of predicted sustained demand, spot or burst for remaining headroom.

4) Reliability initiatives (projects and OKRs)

Current initiatives (2025-Q1/Q2)
- Continuous Batching Improvements (owner: Anika Bose) — Goal: improve average tokens/sec by 18% in production; deliverable: new batching scheduler + canary.
- KV-cache persistent snapshotting (owner: Diego Alvarez) — reduce cold-start latency for long-context models by 40% in dedicated clusters.
- Model fallback policy engine (owner: Marcus Chen) — automated routing to compatible quantized variants when primary model capacity is constrained.

Initiative governance
- Each initiative must publish: scope, success metrics (quantitative), rollout plan, rollback criteria, and error-budget reservation.
- Quarterly reliability review with SRE, Platform, and Product to prioritize top 3 initiatives where reliability ROI is highest.

5) Incident review standards and postmortem template

Incident severity model
- Sev0 (Critical): multi-region outage impacting >50% of production traffic or sustained customer-facing data loss. Immediate IC.
- Sev1 (Major): single-region outage with significant latency or >5% customer error rate for 30+ minutes.
- Sev2 (Minor): localized degradation, partial functionality loss, or operator-only impact.

Postmortem timeline and structure (must be blameless)
- Postmortem draft: within 72 hours of incident mitigation.
- Final postmortem: within 14 days including remediation tickets and owners.
- Required sections: Summary, Timeline (UTC), Impact (customers/metrics), Root cause, Contributing factors, Detection and mitigation, Corrective actions, Follow-ups (tickets with owners), and Lessons learned.

Severity to RCA SLA mapping
- Sev0: RCA and remediation plan within 3 business days.
- Sev1: RCA within 7 business days.
- Sev2: RCA within 21 days.

Blameless language guidance
- Use neutral phrasing: e.g., "a service failed to scale due to missing autoscaler constraint" versus blaming an individual.
- Focus on systemic fixes: tests, alerts, documentation, runbook improvements.

6) Operational tooling and dashboards

Canonical dashboards and alerts
- Production API Health (Grafana): availability, p95/p99 latency, error rate by route. Dashboard ID: grafana-prod-api-01.
- Capacity Planner (Looker Studio): rolling 12-week forecast, per-cluster utilization and headroom.
- Error Budget Manager (internal service): shows current burn, projected burn curves, suggested mitigations. Endpoint: https://internal.redwood.com/error-budget

Alerting guardrails
- Pager duty for action-level alerts (oncall); Slack for informative/warning alerts.
- No alert should fire for more than 5% of incidents as repetitive noise. If it does, review and re-tune thresholds.

Developer tools and self-service
- Infra-as-code modules (Terraform): module names: tf-redwood/gke-inference, tf-redwood/gpu-autoscaler. Repo: git@github.com:redwood/infrastructure.git.
- SRE runbook CLI: rdb-runbook (internal tool) e.g., rdb-runbook run api-high-latency --dry-run.
- Canary harness: load-gen scripts and example config under /ops/canary-load-tests.

7) Runbooks (canonical)

A. Runbook: API high-latency (oncall checklist)
1. Confirm alert: open Grafana "Production API Health" panel and check p95/p99 and error rate.
2. Verify scope: is it single-region or multi-region? Check region label in metrics.
3. Check recent deploys: git commits in the last 60 minutes (git log --since='60 minutes' origin/main). If a suspected deployment, rollback via CI: 
   - CI rollback: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $CI_TOKEN" https://ci.redwood.com/api/v1/rollback -d '{"service":"api-server","to":"previous"}'
4. Identify resource pressure: check node GPU utilization (kubectl top pods -n inference) and autoscaler events (kubectl get events -n inference --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp).
5. Apply mitigation: scale replicas (kubectl scale deployment api-server --replicas=XX -n inference) or enable traffic shaping to reduce non-critical routes.
6. If error budget burn > 25% in 7d, escalate to PD and trigger cross-team IC.
7. Post-incident: if a human action fixed the issue, add an automated check or alert to detect the condition preemptively.

B. Runbook: GPU OOM / node eviction
1. Detect: nodename and pod metric show OOM kills (kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Failed).
2. Quarantine node: cordon node (kubectl cordon <node>) and drain if necessary (kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data).
3. Collect diagnostics: journalctl -u nvidia-driver, /var/log/syslog, dmesg; save to S3: aws s3 cp /tmp/node-<node>-diag.tgz s3://redwood-diagnostics/$INCIDENT_ID/
4. Restart scheduler or redeploy model instances with lower batch size; update model config through admin panel to reduce memory per-worker.
5. File ticket to infra team for hardware replacement if driver/kernel issue is confirmed.

8) Playbook maintenance and ownership
- Document owner (this page): Marcus Chen. Maintain cadence: update after any Sev1/Sev0 event or quarterly.
- Reviewers: SRE leads, Platform PO, and Security when changes touch access controls.
- Labels and lifecycle: tag runbooks with a last-verified date in the page header.
